lessons.title: What is HTML?
lessons.body:
HTML (HyperText Markup Language) is the skeleton of the web. It uses tags like

,

,

, and to define structure. Every page starts with and wraps content in .

lessons.title: Document Structure
lessons.body: Every page has <head> (metadata, title, CSS links) and <body> (what users see). The head is invisible; the body is everything.

lessons.title: Headings & Paragraphs
lessons.body:
Use

through

for headings — h1 is biggest. Wrap text in

for paragraphs. Browsers add spacing automatically.

lessons.title: Links & Images
lessons.body: Links: click. Images: . The alt text describes the image for accessibility.

lessons.title: Lists & Tables
lessons.body:
Unordered list:
  • item
. Ordered:
    . Tables:
    cell
    . Use for structured data only.

lessons.title: Forms & Inputs
lessons.body: Forms collect user input. <form><input type="text"><button>Submit</button></form>. Input types: text, email, password, number, checkbox, radio.

lessons.title: What is CSS?
lessons.body: CSS (Cascading Style Sheets) controls how HTML looks. Link it via <link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css"> in the head.

lessons.title: Selectors
lessons.body: Tag: p { color: red; }. Class: .btn { padding: 10px; }. ID: #header { height: 60px; }. Classes are reusable; IDs must be unique.

lessons.title: Box Model
lessons.body: Every element is a box: content → padding (inside space) → border → margin (outside space). Understand this and layout becomes easy.

lessons.title: Flexbox
lessons.body: display: flex turns a container into a flexible row or column. justify-content: center centers horizontally. align-items: center centers vertically.

lessons.title: Grid
lessons.body: display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr 1fr creates 3 equal columns. Grid is best for full page layouts.

lessons.title: Responsive Design
lessons.body: @media (max-width: 600px) { nav { flex-direction: column; } } — media queries change styles based on screen size.

lessons.title: What is JavaScript?
lessons.body: JavaScript makes pages interactive. It handles clicks, form submissions, animations, and API calls. Add via <script src="app.js"></script>.

lessons.title: Variables
lessons.body: let name = "Lisa"; (changeable). const PI = 3.14; (fixed). var is old — don't use it.

lessons.title: Data Types
lessons.body: String: "hello". Number: 42. Boolean: true. Array: [1,2,3]. Object: { name: "Lisa", age: 19 }. Null and undefined are empty values.

lessons.title: Functions
lessons.body: function greet(name) { return "Hi " + name; }. Arrow version: const greet = (name) => "Hi " + name. Functions are reusable logic blocks.

lessons.title: Loops
lessons.body: for (let i = 0; i < 5; i++) { console.log(i); }. Also: forEach, map, filter, while, do-while.

lessons.title: Conditionals
lessons.body: if (age >= 18) { adult(); } else if (age >= 13) { teen(); } else { child(); }. Switch statements handle many cases cleanly.

lessons.title: What is the DOM?
lessons.body: The DOM (Document Object Model) is the browser's live tree of your HTML. JavaScript can read and change it in real time.

lessons.title: Selecting Elements
lessons.body: document.getElementById("id") — by id. document.querySelector(".class") — first match. document.querySelectorAll("p") — all paragraphs.

lessons.title: Changing Content
lessons.body: element.textContent = "new"; element.innerHTML = "bold"; element.style.color = "red"; element.classList.add("active");

lessons.title: Events
lessons.body: button.addEventListener("click", () => { alert("hi"); });. Common events: click, input, submit, keydown, scroll, focus, blur.

lessons.title: Forms & preventDefault
lessons.body: form.addEventListener("submit", (e) => { e.preventDefault(); const data = new FormData(form); });. preventDefault stops page reload.

lessons.title: Practice Project
lessons.body: Build a to-do app: input field, add button, list. Click adds a task. Click on task removes it. Save tasks to localStorage so they persist.

lessons.title: What is Git?
lessons.body: Git tracks every change to your code. Each save is a commit. You can rewind, compare, branch off, and collaborate without breaking main.

lessons.title: Setup
lessons.body: Install from git-scm.com. Set identity: git config --global user.name "Your Name" and git config --global user.email "you@x.com".

lessons.title: Basic Commands
lessons.body: git init (start repo). git add . (stage all). git commit -m "msg" (save). git push (upload). git pull (download). git status (see state).

lessons.title: Branches
lessons.body: git checkout -b feature (create + switch). git checkout main (back). git merge feature (combine). Branches let you work safely.

lessons.title: GitHub
lessons.body: GitHub hosts repos online. Create repo → connect with git remote add origin URL → git push -u origin main. All deploy platforms pull from GitHub.

lessons.title: Pull Requests
lessons.body: A PR is 'please review my branch'. Standard on teams. Reviewers comment, request changes, then merge.

lessons.title: What is Node?
lessons.body: Node lets you run JavaScript on the server — outside the browser. Same language, different environment. Download from nodejs.org. Check: node -v.

lessons.title: NPM
lessons.body: NPM is Node's package manager. npm init -y creates package.json. npm install express adds a library. node_modules holds installed packages.

lessons.title: First Server
lessons.body: const express = require('express'); const app = express(); app.get('/', (req, res) => res.send('hi')); app.listen(3000);

lessons.title: Routes
lessons.body: app.get('/users') lists. app.post('/users') creates. app.put('/users/:id') updates. app.delete('/users/:id') removes. REST convention.

lessons.title: Middleware
lessons.body: app.use(express.json()) parses JSON bodies. Custom: app.use((req,res,next) => { console.log(req.url); next(); }). Runs before routes.

lessons.title: Deploy
lessons.body: Push to GitHub. Deploy on Render, Railway, Fly.io, or Koyeb. Server runs 24/7 reachable from anywhere. Set env vars for secrets.

lessons.title: What is Python?
lessons.body: Python is a readable, general-purpose language used for web, data, automation, AI, and scripting. Install from python.org. Check: python --version.

lessons.title: Variables & Types
lessons.body: name = "Lisa". age = 19. pi = 3.14. active = True. items = [1,2,3]. person = {"name": "Lisa"}. Python is dynamically typed.

lessons.title: Control Flow
lessons.body: if age >= 18: print("adult"). else: print("minor"). Indentation matters. for i in range(5): print(i). while x < 10: x += 1.

lessons.title: Functions
lessons.body: def greet(name): return f"Hi {name}". f-strings format values inline. Default args: def greet(name="world"):. Return multiple: return a, b.

lessons.title: Files & Modules
lessons.body: with open('file.txt', 'r') as f: content = f.read(). Import: import os, sys, json, requests. Install packages: pip install requests.

lessons.title: Practice
lessons.body: Build a script that reads a CSV of names, filters by age > 30, and writes the result to a new CSV. Real automation skill.

lessons.title: Why Databases?
lessons.body: Files don't scale. Databases handle millions of records, concurrent users, and fast queries with indexes.

lessons.title: Tables & Rows
lessons.body: A database has tables. A table has columns (fields) and rows (records). Primary key = unique id per row. Foreign key = reference to another table.

lessons.title: SELECT
lessons.body: SELECT * FROM users; (all). SELECT name, email FROM users WHERE age > 18; (filtered). SELECT COUNT(*) FROM users; (count).

lessons.title: INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE
lessons.body: INSERT INTO users (name, email) VALUES ('Lisa', 'l@x.com');. UPDATE users SET name='New' WHERE id=1;. DELETE FROM users WHERE id=1;.

lessons.title: JOINs
lessons.body: SELECT u.name, c.title FROM users u JOIN courses c ON c.user_id = u.id;. JOIN links data across tables by a shared column.

lessons.title: Postgres vs SQLite
lessons.body: SQLite: single file, zero setup, great for dev and small apps. Postgres: production-grade, handles heavy traffic, concurrent writes, replicas.

lessons.title: What is Linux?
lessons.body: Linux is a free, open-source OS powering most servers, Android, and cloud. Learn it and you control any server you'll ever touch.

lessons.title: File System
lessons.body: / is root. /home/user for user files. /etc for configs. /var for logs. /tmp for temp. /usr for programs. Everything is a file.

lessons.title: Navigation
lessons.body: pwd (where am I). ls -la (list all). cd /path (change). mkdir new (create folder). rm -rf dir (delete — dangerous!). cp, mv, touch.

lessons.title: File Operations
lessons.body: cat file (view). less file (scroll). head/tail (first/last lines). grep 'text' file (search). chmod 755 file (permissions). chown user file.

lessons.title: Processes
lessons.body: ps aux (list processes). top (live monitor). kill PID (stop). kill -9 PID (force). nohup cmd & (background). systemctl start/stop/status service.

lessons.title: Package Management
lessons.body: Debian/Ubuntu: apt update && apt install pkg. Red Hat/CentOS: yum install pkg. Arch: pacman -S pkg.

lessons.title: OSI Model
lessons.body: 7 layers: Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, Application. Each handles a specific job in getting data across.

lessons.title: TCP vs UDP
lessons.body: TCP is reliable — handshake, ordering, retransmit. UDP is fast and lossy — video, games, DNS. TCP for correctness, UDP for speed.

lessons.title: IP Addresses
lessons.body: IPv4: 192.168.1.1. IPv6: longer hex format. Private ranges: 10.x, 172.16-31.x, 192.168.x. Public addresses route on the internet.

lessons.title: DNS
lessons.body: DNS turns names into IPs. darkloner.com → 76.76.21.21. Records: A (IPv4), AAAA (IPv6), CNAME (alias), MX (mail), TXT (verification).

lessons.title: HTTP/HTTPS
lessons.body: HTTP is the web's language: GET, POST, PUT, DELETE. HTTPS wraps it in TLS encryption. Never run production without HTTPS.

lessons.title: Ports
lessons.body: 22 SSH · 25 SMTP · 53 DNS · 80 HTTP · 443 HTTPS · 3306 MySQL · 5432 Postgres. Know what's open on your systems.

lessons.title: Rules of Engagement
lessons.body: Only test systems you own or have WRITTEN permission for. Get scope in writing. Never touch production data. Ever.

lessons.title: Passive Recon
lessons.body: OSINT without touching the target: WHOIS, Shodan, dnsdumpster, LinkedIn, Google dorks, certificate transparency logs.

lessons.title: Active Recon
lessons.body: Directly touching the target: nmap port scans, banner grabbing, directory busting (gobuster, feroxbuster). Louder, but more info.

lessons.title: Vulnerability Scanning
lessons.body: Nessus, OpenVAS, Nikto flag potential issues. Automated tools are starting points — manual verification is required.

lessons.title: Exploitation
lessons.body: Match vuln to exploit. Test in scope. Document proof (screenshot, log). Never exceed your authorization. Stop when done.

lessons.title: Reporting
lessons.body: Executive summary (business impact), technical findings (CVSS scores), reproduction steps, remediation. The report is the deliverable.

lessons.title: SQL Injection
lessons.body: User input reaches a SQL query unchecked. ' OR 1=1 -- bypasses login. Fix: parameterized queries. Never concatenate user input into SQL.

lessons.title: XSS
lessons.body: Injected JavaScript runs in another user's browser. Steals cookies, hijacks sessions. Fix: escape output, sanitize input, use CSP headers.

lessons.title: CSRF
lessons.body: Trick a logged-in user into making an unwanted request. Fix: CSRF tokens on forms, SameSite=Strict cookies.

lessons.title: IDOR
lessons.body: Change /user/123 to /user/124 and see someone else's data. Fix: server checks ownership on every request, not just the session.

lessons.title: File Uploads
lessons.body: Unrestricted upload = remote code execution. Fix: whitelist extensions, rename files, store outside webroot, scan contents.

lessons.title: SSRF
lessons.body: Server fetches a URL the attacker controls, hits internal services. Fix: whitelist allowed hosts, block internal IPs (169.254.x, 10.x, 127.x).

lessons.title: What is React?
lessons.body: React is a JavaScript library for building UIs from components. Component = function that returns JSX. Everything is composable.

lessons.title: JSX
lessons.body:
JSX looks like HTML inside JS: const el =

Hello

. It compiles to React.createElement calls. Use {} to embed JS:

{name}

.

lessons.title: Components & Props
lessons.body:
function Card({ title, body }) { return

{title}

{body}

; }. Props are inputs. Read-only inside the component.

lessons.title: State with useState
lessons.body: const [count, setCount] = useState(0);. setCount(count + 1) triggers re-render. State is component memory.

lessons.title: useEffect
lessons.body: useEffect(() => { fetch('/api').then(...); }, []);. Runs after render. Empty array = once. [dep] = when dep changes.

lessons.title: Lists & Keys
lessons.body:
{items.map(i =>
  • {i.name}
    • )}. Key must be unique and stable. Helps React track which items changed.

lessons.title: What is Docker?
lessons.body: Docker packages your app + dependencies into a portable container. Same behavior on laptop, server, cloud. Ends 'it works on my machine'.

lessons.title: Images vs Containers
lessons.body: Image = blueprint (read-only). Container = running instance of an image. Build once, run many. Images stored in registries (Docker Hub).

lessons.title: Dockerfile
lessons.body: FROM node:20. WORKDIR /app. COPY . . RUN npm install. CMD ["node", "index.js"]. Each line is a layer, cached between builds.

lessons.title: Commands
lessons.body: docker build -t myapp . (build). docker run -p 3000:3000 myapp (run). docker ps (list running). docker logs ID (see output). docker exec -it ID sh (shell in).

lessons.title: Volumes
lessons.body: docker run -v /host:/container myapp. Persists data outside the container. Essential for databases.

lessons.title: Docker Compose
lessons.body: docker-compose.yml defines multi-container apps. One file for app + DB + cache. docker compose up starts everything.

lessons.title: What is Cloud?
lessons.body: Renting computers by the second instead of buying servers. Pay for what you use. Scale up in minutes. Global regions.

lessons.title: Core Services
lessons.body: Compute: EC2 (VM), Lambda (serverless). Storage: S3, GCS. Database: RDS, DynamoDB, Firestore. Networking: VPC, Route 53.

lessons.title: IAM
lessons.body: Identity and Access Management controls who can do what. Users, groups, roles, policies. Least privilege — give minimum needed access.

lessons.title: Deploying
lessons.body: Push code → CI/CD builds → uploads to cloud → runs behind load balancer. Services: AWS CodePipeline, GCP Cloud Build, GitHub Actions.

lessons.title: Cost Control
lessons.body: Watch for: idle instances, oversized VMs, forgotten snapshots, egress bandwidth. Set billing alerts. Kill unused resources weekly.

lessons.title: Practice
lessons.body: Deploy a simple Node app to AWS Lightsail or GCP Compute. Connect a domain. Set up HTTPS. That's a real cloud skill.

lessons.title: CIA Triad
lessons.body: Confidentiality (only authorized see data). Integrity (no tampering). Availability (stays up for users). Every security decision balances these three.

lessons.title: Threat Modeling
lessons.body: Who attacks? Why? What access? What's the impact? Map it on paper. STRIDE: Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Info disclosure, DoS, Elevation.

lessons.title: OWASP Top 10
lessons.body: 1. Broken Access · 2. Crypto failures · 3. Injection · 4. Insecure design · 5. Misconfig · 6. Vulnerable components · 7. Auth failures · 8. Integrity · 9. Logging · 10. SSRF.

lessons.title: Defense in Depth
lessons.body: Multiple layers: firewall, WAF, MFA, patching, backups, logging, monitoring, incident response, employee training. No single layer is enough.

lessons.title: Incident Response
lessons.body: Prepare → Identify → Contain → Eradicate → Recover → Learn. Have a plan BEFORE you need it. Document everything.

lessons.title: Practice
lessons.body: Take a website you built. Walk through OWASP Top 10. Mark which apply. Fix one vulnerability and document the fix.

lessons.title: Why TypeScript?
lessons.body: TS adds types to JS. Catch bugs at compile time instead of runtime. Better IDE autocomplete. Scales to large teams.

lessons.title: Basic Types
lessons.body: let name: string = "Lisa". let age: number = 19. let active: boolean = true. let items: string[] = []. let data: any — avoid.

lessons.title: Interfaces
lessons.body: interface User { id: number; name: string; email?: string; }. ? means optional. Objects must match or TS errors.

lessons.title: Functions
lessons.body: function greet(name: string): string { return `Hi ${name}`; }. Specify param types and return type. TypeScript enforces contracts.

lessons.title: Generics
lessons.body: function identity<T>(x: T): T { return x; }. Works with any type but keeps type safety. Used heavily in React and APIs.

lessons.title: Setup
lessons.body: npm install -g typescript. tsconfig.json configures the compiler. tsc file.ts compiles to file.js. Use with React via create-react-app --template typescript.

lessons.title: What is MongoDB?
lessons.body: MongoDB stores JSON-like documents (BSON) instead of rows. Flexible schema. Great for evolving data and rapid prototyping.

lessons.title: Collections & Documents
lessons.body: Database → Collections → Documents. A document is like a row but can have nested objects and arrays. Each has a unique _id.

lessons.title: Queries
lessons.body: db.users.find({ age: { $gt: 18 } }). db.users.findOne({ email: 'x@y.com' }). db.users.insertOne({ name: 'Lisa' }).

lessons.title: Update & Delete
lessons.body: db.users.updateOne({ _id: 1 }, { $set: { name: 'New' } }). db.users.deleteOne({ _id: 1 }). deleteMany for bulk.

lessons.title: Aggregation
lessons.body: db.orders.aggregate([{ $group: { _id: '$user', total: { $sum: '$amount' } } }]). Powerful pipeline for stats and reports.

lessons.title: Mongoose (Node)
lessons.body: const schema = new mongoose.Schema({ name: String, email: String }); const User = mongoose.model('User', schema);. Schema validation + ODM.

lessons.title: What is FastAPI?
lessons.body: FastAPI is a modern Python web framework. Auto docs, type hints, async support, blazing fast. Great for APIs and microservices.

lessons.title: Install & Hello
lessons.body: pip install fastapi uvicorn. from fastapi import FastAPI; app = FastAPI(); @app.get('/') def home(): return {'msg': 'hi'}. Run: uvicorn main:app --reload.

lessons.title: Path & Query Params
lessons.body: @app.get('/users/{id}') def get(id: int): return {'id': id}. Query params: def search(q: str = None). FastAPI validates automatically.

lessons.title: POST with Pydantic
lessons.body: from pydantic import BaseModel; class User(BaseModel): name: str; email: str. @app.post('/users') def create(u: User): return u. Auto validation.

lessons.title: Auth
lessons.body: JWT in FastAPI: pip install python-jose passlib. Create token on login, verify on protected routes with Depends().

lessons.title: Docs
lessons.body: Go to /docs — interactive Swagger UI. Every endpoint listed. Try requests live. Built-in OpenAPI schema at /openapi.json.

lessons.title: Getting Started
lessons.body: You don't need permission. Build 3 projects. Put them on GitHub. Create a simple portfolio. Start telling people you build websites.

lessons.title: Finding Clients
lessons.body: Fiverr/Upwork for practice. Local businesses for real money. Twitter/LinkedIn for inbound. Referrals are the best long-term channel.

lessons.title: Pricing
lessons.body: Simple site: $200–800. Business site: $800–3000. Web app: $3000+. Always 50% upfront, 50% on delivery. Hourly for ongoing work.

lessons.title: Contracts
lessons.body: Always written. Scope, timeline, price, revisions, payment terms, IP ownership, kill fee. Use a template — don't reinvent.

lessons.title: Communication
lessons.body: Weekly updates. Screenshots. Ask questions early. Say no to scope creep or charge for it. Over-communicate to prevent disasters.

lessons.title: Handoff
lessons.body: Deliver source files. Give admin access. Train the client. Charge for maintenance or offer a retainer. Document everything.
